title: Telegram
rule: All captions in telegraphese: no articles, every sentence ends STOP.
declares: keeps E0-E5, the four lines and the outcome
build: films/swarm/99-ways/build/p94_telegram.py (cut paper: kit/cutpaper99.py; agent and clock: kit/build_page02.py; stranger: build/p64_window_in_window.woman; cupboard, key, memo, window, SERVICE door: build/p86_picture_book.py helpers)

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

made: the page is a station telegraph blank of our own invention (no real company's name or mark): one large HANDMADE cut sheet of buff paper with 'TELEGRAM' cut from brown paper and its printed heads in brown pen ink (STATION WIRE - DAY MESSAGE - FORM 94; FROM: AGENT, RANDOLPH VT.; TO: DIVISION OFFICE; SEPT 1937 4:16 PM)

six cut-paper pictures on scissor-cut cards in muted office papers: page 02's cut-paper agent and clock (4:10), page 64's cut-paper stranger, page 86's cupboard (open on the left jamb), brass key with SERVICE tag, memo slip and blue SERVICE door
the captions: lengths of telegraph tape (HANDMADE cut strips of pale paper, each end cut askew, one paper shadow) pasted one sentence per strip, lettered in capitals in the shared pen hand
the four canon lines verbatim in cut-paper balloons inside the pictures (speech, not captions)
captions: MEMO SAYS OPEN SERVICE DOOR 4:15 STOP
AGENT RISES TO FETCH IT STOP
STRANGER AT TICKET WINDOW ASKS TIME STOP
BRASS KEY ON HOOK TAGGED SERVICE STOP

events.E4: picture 5: open cupboard, key tagged SERVICE
events.E5: picture 6: forgetting; tapes give the outcome

beat: the wire comes in: the blank first, then each picture is pasted and its tapes are pasted under it, strip by strip

self_check.check: Every caption sentence ends with STOP; no 'a' or 'the' appears in the captions.
self_check.evidence: checked in code (p94_telegram.check_caps: every strip ends ' STOP', no word a/an/the) and by eye on the full page
self_check.pending: independent blind reading not run by the maker

weaknesses: the balloons keep the canon lines with their articles ('the right time', 'the clock'); the rule is read as applying to captions only
the figures and props are the same cut-paper kit as page 86, so the pictures look close to that page; the telegram blank and tapes carry the difference
the form header ('STATION WIRE', 'DIVISION OFFICE', '4:16 PM') is invented furniture, not caption; it also has no articles
the agent's 'walk' pose in picture 1 reads more as standing than rising
